With a zero-delay retry, the phase is never set to 'retrying'. A cancel issued from an abort listener or any reentrant path during the window sees the phase as 'running' with an already-ended attempt. Probably unreachable today, but the invariant is fragile.
A re-entrant cancel during a timed-out attempt's abort can still deliver the queued 'retry' event after the task is cancelled.
Cycle detection walks every node reachable from the new task's deps on every add, so cost is O(V+E) per add and quadratic when building large graphs (a performance issue, not a correctness bug)
emit() queues a closure that snapshots the listener set at delivery time, not at emit time, so a listener subscribed between queueing and flush receives an event that predates its subscription
